title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #4 (Term 1)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the seed activity, why do we plant two tins? (1 mark)
   A. To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   B. To use up all the soil
   C. Because one tin is too small
   D. To make it look neat

2. Which sacred plant belongs to Buddhist tradition because of the Buddha's enlightenment? (1 mark)
   A. Tulsi
   B. Bodhi tree
   C. Ber tree
   D. Sal tree

3. Which tree is linked with Lord Mahavir's enlightenment? (1 mark)
   A. Banana tree
   B. Ber tree
   C. Sal tree
   D. Tulsi

4. Which Sanskrit word means water? (1 mark)
   A. Prithvi
   B. Vayu
   C. Jal
   D. Agni

5. Which tree is linked with Guru Nanak Dev Ji at Sultanpur Lodhi? (1 mark)
   A. Ber (Beri) tree
   B. Sal tree
   C. Bodhi tree
   D. Tulsi

6. Where did Prince Siddhartha sit under the Bodhi tree? (1 mark)
   A. Bodh Gaya
   B. Nairobi
   C. Amritsar
   D. Lumbini

7. Which medical use of Tulsi is mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A fuel for cars
   B. A cloth
   C. Tea for coughs and colds
   D. A tool for digging

8. Sri Guru Ram Das Ji was which Guru of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. The first
   B. The fourth
   C. The third
   D. The tenth

9. Which activity helps us remember the teachings of Enlightened Beings? (1 mark)
   A. Acting a skit of a story
   B. Reading the story aloud twice
   C. Colouring the poster
   D. Reading it silently

10. What does Aparigraha mean? (1 mark)
   A. Always be angry
   B. Take everything
   C. Talk a lot
   D. Do not be greedy or hold too many things

11. What does the story of the swan teach us? (1 mark)
   A. To hunt for fun
   B. To be kind to animals and help the hurt
   C. To ignore suffering
   D. To be proud

12. Which Tirthankar is the twenty-third of Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. Mahavir
   B. Parshvanath
   C. Guru Nanak
   D. Buddha

13. Where was Hiranyakashipu when Narsimha stopped him? (1 mark)
   A. On a boat
   B. At the doorway, neither inside nor outside
   C. In a field
   D. On a mountain

14. How did Prahlad react when his father was angry? (1 mark)
   A. He gave up praying
   B. He stayed calm and kept his faith
   C. He ran away forever
   D. He became cruel

15. Who brought Siddhartha up after his mother died? (1 mark)
   A. His cousin Devadatta
   B. A king
   C. A teacher
   D. His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami

16. How can you learn more about scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Copy them from memory only
   B. Listen to a resource person or visit a library
   C. Keep them in a bag
   D. Ignore them

17. Who declared that Sikhs should follow the Granth as their Guru? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   B. Sigala
   C. Ram
   D. Guru Amar Das Ji

18. Which pair is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Ramayan: Buddhism
   B. Dhammapada: Sikhism
   C. Kalpasutra: Hinduism
   D. Uttaradhyayan Sutra: Jainism

19. For how many years was Ram asked to live in the forest? (1 mark)
   A. Fifty
   B. Fourteen
   C. Two
   D. Five

20. Which scripture is a Jain book about the life of Lord Mahavir? (1 mark)
   A. Kalpasutra
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Guru Granth Sahib
   D. Ramayan

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how Sikhs show respect to Guru Granth Sahib Ji in a gurdwara. (3 marks)

22. What does the name Narsimha mean? (2 marks)

23. Who compiled Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji first, and who declared it the eternal Guru? (2 marks)

24. Explain what the Sigalovada Sutta teaches about the six directions. (3 marks)

25. Describe the early life of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji. (4 marks)

26. Tell the story of the Ayodhya Kaand in three sentences. (3 marks)

27. Explain the meaning of Ahimsa and give two ways to practise it. (3 marks)

28. Describe how Hindu families care for the Tulsi plant. (3 marks)

29. Give two of Parshvanath's four rules. (2 marks)

30. Discuss how people of different faiths show respect for water and trees. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — To compare seeds with water and seeds without water
   Comparing shows that water is needed for growth.

2. B — Bodhi tree
   Bodhi tree is the tree of awakening.

3. C — Sal tree
   Jains say Lord Mahavir became enlightened under a sal tree.

4. C — Jal
   Jal (also Apas) means water.

5. A — Ber (Beri) tree
   The Ber Sahib stands beside a gurdwara in Sultanpur Lodhi.

6. A — Bodh Gaya
   He became the Buddha at Bodh Gaya.

7. C — Tea for coughs and colds
   Tulsi leaves are used in home medicine such as tea.

8. B — The fourth
   He came after Guru Amar Das Ji.

9. A — Acting a skit of a story
   A skit helps us learn the lesson.

10. D — Do not be greedy or hold too many things
   Aparigraha is non-greed.

11. B — To be kind to animals and help the hurt
   Siddhartha showed kindness.

12. B — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is the twenty-third Tirthankar.

13. B — At the doorway, neither inside nor outside
   Narsimha stopped him at the threshold.

14. B — He stayed calm and kept his faith
   Prahlad kept his faith without fear.

15. D — His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami
   His mother's sister looked after him.

16. B — Listen to a resource person or visit a library
   We can listen, read and discuss.

17. A — Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   He was the tenth Guru.

18. D — Uttaradhyayan Sutra: Jainism
   The Uttaradhyayan Sutra is a Jain scripture.

19. B — Fourteen
   Kaikeyi asked that Ram go for fourteen years.

20. A — Kalpasutra
   The Kalpasutra tells the life of Lord Mahavir.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is placed on a raised seat; people cover their heads, remove shoes and bow before it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Man-lion, from nar (man) and simha (lion).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled it; Guru Gobind Singh Ji declared it the Guru.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: It tells us to respect and care for parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and helpers, and holy teachers, and they in turn care for us.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming groups, 1 mark for respect and care, 1 mark for mutual duty.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: He was born in Lahore with the childhood name Jetha, lost his parents young, helped his family by selling boiled grain, and later served Guru Amar Das Ji.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 4.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dasharatha was about to hand the kingdom to Ram, but Kaikeyi asked that Bharat be king and Ram go to the forest for fourteen years. Ram accepted calmly and left with Sita and Lakshman. Bharat placed Ram's sandals on the throne and ruled in his name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ahimsa is not harming any living being by thought, word or action. We practise it by not bullying and by caring for animals and plants.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow it in a pot or a stand in the courtyard, water it every morning, walk around it and pray. Its leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna and used in home medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 3.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya or Aparigraha (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

30. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hindus honour the Ganga and Tulsi; Sikhs remember the Beas and the Ber tree; Jains honour the Rijubalika and the Sal tree; Buddhists honour the Bodhi tree. All value water and trees and take care of them.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each faith correctly described, up to 4 marks, and 1 mark for the idea that all faiths show respect.
